page: Microsoft Azure E1ps_v7 is an entry-level memory-optimized instance within the Epsv7 family, running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an arm64 processor architecture and provides 1 dedicated virtual CPU along with 8.0 GB of memory. This configuration establishes a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, aligning directly with memory-intensive operational requirements. The virtual machine does not include integrated hardware graphics acceleration, operating with zero GPUs.

Regarding storage and connectivity, the E1ps_v7 does not include local ephemeral storage disks. Instead, it relies on network-attached storage architectures, supporting Azure Premium Storage volumes to handle persistent system and application data. Network configurations do not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating virtual network gateways or dedicated IP allocations for inbound and outbound routing.

With a single dedicated ARM core and 8.0 GB of system memory, the resource profile suits lightweight applications that require elevated memory capacity relative to compute power. Primary use cases include small in-memory key-value stores, memory-caching daemons, lightweight relational databases, and low-traffic microservices built for the arm64 instruction set. However, processing throughput is constrained by the single vCPU configuration, making it unsuited for multi-threaded processing or compute-heavy analytical tasks.
description: The Microsoft Azure E1ps_v7 is an entry-tier memory-optimized virtual machine built on an arm64 processor architecture within the Epsv7 family. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provisions 1 dedicated vCPU paired with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core allocation. The server includes no GPUs and contains no local storage volumes, relying on attached Azure Premium Storage disks for persistent block storage. Network routing does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Due to its single-core configuration and generous memory allocation relative to compute, the E1ps_v7 provides a cost-efficient memory footprint for memory-dependent tasks that do not demand extensive CPU throughput. It is technically suited for small in-memory caches, low-demand database instances, ARM-native microservices, and background data routing tasks.
